title: Geometrically connected fibres of proper maps to normal schemes
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that $S$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and normal: every local ring of $S$ is an integrally closed domain. Assume that $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], that every generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] maps to $\xi$, and that the structure map induces $H^0(X_\xi,\mathcal O_{X_\xi})=\kappa(\xi)$ as $\kappa(\xi)$-algebras [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then the canonical map $\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ is an isomorphism and every fibre of $f$ is geometrically connected: for every $s\in S$ and every field extension $L/\kappa(s)$, the scheme $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}L$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. No Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, all six hypotheses and both conclusions.

proof.text: Work over an arbitrary nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$. It contains $\xi$, since its complement is closed and cannot contain the generic point unless it is all of $S$. Put $Y=f^{-1}(U)$ and $g:Y\to U$. The morphism $g$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), and $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. It is reduced because its local rings are local rings of $X$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The ring $A$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Put $K=\kappa(\xi)$; [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2) identifies the stalk at $\xi$ with the fraction field of $A$, so its maximal ideal is zero and its residue field $K$ is that same fraction field. In particular $A\to K$ is injective. The generic fibre $Y_\xi$ is canonically $X_\xi$, since $\xi\in U$.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal; affine-local preparation for the proof

proof.text: The ring $A$ is integrally closed in $K$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](1) identifies every $A_{\mathfrak p}$ with the local ring of $S$ at the corresponding point of $U$. These are integrally closed domains by hypothesis, so $A$ is a normal ring in precisely the sense of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. A domain is reduced and its only minimal prime is $(0)$, since $(0)$ is prime and is contained in every prime. Its nonzerodivisors are exactly its nonzero elements, so its total ring of fractions is $K$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions], implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), applies and says that every element of $K$ integral over $A$ belongs to $A$.

source.place: Tag 030C, lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal, (1) implies (2); affine algebra used in Morphisms Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal

proof.text: Set $B=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine] to the proper $g$. It gives the canonical factorization $Y\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{\pi}\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A\to B$ integral and $q$ proper with geometrically connected fibres. In particular no finiteness of $B$ as an $A$-module is being assumed. Restriction to the generic fibre, followed by the assumed structural isomorphism $\Gamma(X_\xi,\mathcal O)=K$, gives an $A$-algebra homomorphism $r:B\to K$ whose composite with $A\to B$ is the inclusion $A\to K$.

source.place: Tag 03H2, theorem-stein-factorization-general, (1), (2), (4), affine case; Tag 0AY8, proof, first sentence

proof.text: The homomorphism $r$ is injective. Let $h\in B$ have $r(h)=0$, so its pullback to $X_\xi$ is the zero section. Given $y\in Y$, choose an irreducible component $C$ of $X$ containing $y$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], and its generic point $\zeta$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Because $Y\subset X$ is open and contains $y\in\overline{\{\zeta\}}$, it contains $\zeta$ too. By hypothesis $f(\zeta)=\xi$. The canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\zeta)\to X$ therefore factors through $X_\xi$, by the residue-field map $\kappa(\xi)\to\kappa(\zeta)$ of [def-weil-residue-field] and the defining fibre product [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Hence $h(\zeta)=0$. The locus where a section has zero residue is closed: on each affine chart of $Y$, it is the closed set $V(h)$. Its complement is the basic open where $h$ is invertible. This closed locus contains $\zeta$, and therefore contains $C\cap Y=\overline{\{\zeta\}}\cap Y$, in particular $y$. Thus $h(y)=0$ for every $y\in Y$. Since $Y$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-qc-scheme-vanishing-section-nilpotent] makes $h$ nilpotent. Since $Y$ is reduced, its section ring is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme], so $h=0$. Applying this to a difference proves injectivity.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, proof, reducedness and dominance of all components; affine verification of the injectivity implicit in the normalization argument

proof.text: For $b\in B$, integrality supplies a monic polynomial over $A$ annihilating $b$. Applying $r$ shows that $r(b)\in K$ is integral over $A$, so Step 2 gives $r(b)=a$ for some $a\in A$. Since $r$ restricts to the inclusion on $A$, injectivity from Step 4 gives $b=\operatorname{image}(a)$. Thus $A\to B$ is surjective. It is also injective, because its composite with $r$ is the injective map $A\to K$. This proves that the canonical structure homomorphism $\mathcal O_S(U)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}U)$ is an isomorphism for every nonempty affine $U$. On an empty affine both section rings are the zero ring. These are the components of the canonical map of sheaves; their inverses commute with restriction by uniqueness of inverses. On any open, use an affine covering, apply the inverses to the local restrictions, and glue: agreement on overlaps can be checked on affine subopens and follows from injectivity there. This constructs an inverse sheaf morphism, proving $\mathcal O_S\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, proof, affine integral-birational-normal argument (Morphisms Tag 0AB1) and the first conclusion

proof.text: Finally fix $s\in S$ and a field extension $L/\kappa(s)$, and choose a nonempty affine $U$ containing $s$. For its factorization in Step 3, the canonical $A\to B$ is the isomorphism just proved, so $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}(A\to B)$ is an isomorphism by the contravariant affine-spectrum construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Under this isomorphism, $g=\pi q$ is identified with $q$. Consequently $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}L$ is the fibre of $q$ after the corresponding field extension, by the defining fibre products. The geometric connectedness conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine](iii) says this scheme is nonempty and connected. Since $s,L$ were arbitrary, this proves the second conclusion.
